newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia's Potanin plans Eurobond, World Bank talks.
newsitem.headline: Russia's Potanin plans Eurobond, World Bank talks.

text.p: First Deputy Prime Minister Vladimir Potanin will fly to New York on Tuesday to discuss Russia's debut Eurobond issue with potential investors and a coal loan with the World Bank, his spokeswoman Larisa Zelkova said on Monday.

Russian officials are currently conducting a road-show for the Eurobond in international financial centres. The government has ordered the dollar-denominated paper to be issued by the end of this year.
Potanin, who is in charge of economy, also plans to meet World Bank representatives for talks on a new tranche of a $500 million loan for Russia's coal industry, Zelkova told Reuters.
"Potanin wants to meet senior officials at the World Bank to discuss new loans for the Russian economy, including a new tranche of the $500 million credit for the coal industry," she said.
Caio Koch-Weser, managing director, operations, at the World Bank, said earlier this month Russia could get more loans to support economic reforms if more was done to implement existing programmes.
The bank agreed the coal loan, to be paid in two equal tranches, earlier this year, but Russian officials said the second tranche was under threat as the first had not been used.

Bank officials complained Russia had not carried out a necessary audit of coal companies and that restructuring was proceeding too slowly. Funds had not been paid to the regions to help cushion the restructuring under the terms of the loan.
The World Bank board agreed to review the implementation of the terms in November.
"Potanin hopes to meet Koch-Weser and clarify the situation with the coal loan," Zelkova said.
